ai.description: *Boiga andamanensis* is a slender, arboreal colubrid reaching 1.5m. It features a reddish-brown body with dark crossbands and a distinct, triangular head with a blunt snout and large, golden eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga andamanensis* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid yellow-and-black checkered belly, which contrasts sharply with the plain or uniform ventrals of other Indian *Boiga*.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Cat Snake inhabits the dense tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found in low-to-mid elevation canopy vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, using its slender body to navigate tree branches while hunting for small vertebrates under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga andamanensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–10 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring from sea level up to approximately 700 meters within tropical forest habitats.
